@copilot Reduce the testing added by this PR to basic SDK integration coverage of the new DynamoDB terminal-error classification. This is a test-scope reduction, not a request to change production behavior.

Keep DynamoDbErrorsTest.sdkProtocolOutcome() with both existing parameter rows: an actual instrumented DynamoDbClient call receiving ResourceNotFoundException must emit ERROR and error.type=ResourceNotFoundException on its span and existing db.client.operation.duration metric, and a missing item must remain successful. Controlled HTTP responses are fine; keep the real SDK/interceptor path rather than constructing an instrumenter invocation manually.

Remove finalOutcome(), its errors() constructed-exception matrix, and their unused imports/helpers. Remove the three newly added DynamoDbErrorsV0, DynamoDbErrorsNew, and DynamoDbErrorsDual executions and the test.dynamodb.rpc-semconv mocked GlobalOpenTelemetry/configuration setup and reset code that exists solely for those executions. Preserve pre-existing test suites, configuration coverage, dependency-version coverage, and the pre-existing ExceptionSignalLogs execution.

Preserve exact emitted-telemetry assertions and the production fix. Remove imports, dependencies, or wiring made unused by these deletions. Use the repository's narrow formatting and relevant validation commands, without adding test permutations or unrelated fixes. Keep this deliverable scoped to this existing PR and preserve its draft/ready state. Update the PR description only where the reduced coverage makes it stale, while preserving its repository template. Report exactly what was retained and removed.

replies.body: Retained `sdkProtocolOutcome()` with its real instrumented `DynamoDbClient` error and missing-item cases and exact span/metric assertions. Removed `finalOutcome()`, the constructed-exception matrix, RPC-mode mocking/reset, and the three RPC-mode executions; preserved `ExceptionSignalLogs` and the existing suites and dependency-version coverage. Addressed in `fe88f042`.

threads.body:
@copilot Refactor this PR's DynamoDB terminal-error classification to use DbClientAttributesGetter.getErrorType(...) and the shared DbClientAttributesExtractor instead of writing ERROR_TYPE and duplicating its exception-class fallback in DynamoDbAttributesExtractor.onEnd().

Introduce a DynamoDbAttributesGetter for ExecutionAttributes and Response, move the existing DynamoDB attribute extraction into its corresponding getter methods, and wire DbClientAttributesExtractor.create(getter) into AwsSdkInstrumenterFactory.dynamoDbInstrumenter(). Preserve existing database attribute values and omission rules, table-name extraction, BatchWriteItem operation naming and batch-size behavior, network/server attributes, span naming, metrics, and schema URL.

Have getErrorType return the terminal AwsServiceException's awsErrorDetails().errorCode() when non-null and non-blank, and null otherwise, including when there is no error. Let the shared DB extractor provide the exception-class fallback and write error.type. Keep DB extraction after the shared RPC/HTTP extraction so the terminal DynamoDB classification wins independently of RPC semconv mode. Do not implement this solely in AwsSdkRpcAttributesGetter, since RPC error extraction is preview-gated.

Keep the existing real-SDK DynamoDbErrorsTest.sdkProtocolOutcome() coverage and exact span/metric expectations for ResourceNotFoundException and successful missing-item responses. Do not restore the removed constructed-exception matrix or RPC-mode test executions, or add unrelated changes. Use narrow repository formatting and relevant validation. Keep this work scoped to PR #20705 and preserve its draft/ready state. Update its description only if the refactor makes it stale, preserving any repository template.

replies.body: Refactored DynamoDB extraction to `DynamoDbAttributesGetter` and registered the shared `DbClientAttributesExtractor` after the existing shared extractors. Its getter returns a nonblank AWS error code or null, leaving exception-class fallback and `error.type` writing to the shared extractor. Preserved the existing attributes, batch behavior, server data, span name, metrics, schema URL, and integration assertions. Committed as `7ff5e05f`.
